mainTopic: Food swapping, a חבר preparing חלה and תרומה for an עם הארץ, dealings with גוים, and the story of גניבא
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that the wife of an עם הארץ, who might even steal food, would surely swap food too. רב יוסף pushes this away: she takes only because she thinks she is allowed, like an ox eating while it threshes. Next the גמרא brings a ברייתא: a חבר may not prepare an עם הארץ's חלה or תרומה in purity directly. He may, however, prepare the plain dough or olives in purity, set the holy portion aside in a container, and let the עם הארץ take both. רבי יוחנן explains this was allowed to protect the livelihood of the kneader and the olive presser, and the גמרא shows why both cases are needed. It then explains why we need not worry that the עם הארץ will touch the holy portion: we warn him, he clearly cares, and the oil goes into vessels that cannot become impure. The גמרא then turns to the משנה: one may encourage גוים during שביעית with words only, may greet them, and on their holiday may greet them only quietly. The amud ends with the story of גניבא, who greets רב הונא and רב חסדא as 'kings' with a doubled שלום and refuses to eat before feeding his animal. With that, פרק הניזקין comes to a close.

steps.title: If she steals, surely she swaps too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a source about the wife of an עם הארץ who gives food to another woman. It argues that if she is suspected of stealing, she must also be suspected of swapping food.
steps.simpleTranslation: She gives her food and the other woman eats it. Now, if she actually steals, would she not swap?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a source about the wife of an עם הארץ. It uses that source to argue that swapping food is a general worry, not only a worry with a mother-in-law or an innkeeper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source assumes she might steal from her husband to feed someone. The גמרא reasons that swapping is a smaller step than stealing. So if she is suspected of stealing, she should surely be suspected of swapping.

keyTerms.meaning: now, if so (introduces a 'how much more so' argument)

phrases.english: She gives her, and she eats.
Now, if she actually steals,
would she not swap?!

steps.triggerLanguage: השתא מיגנב גנבא חלופי לא מיחלפא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from a source quoted just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only certain people, like a mother-in-law or an innkeeper, are suspected of swapping food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stealing is worse than swapping. Someone suspected of the worse act is surely suspected of the lesser one.

steps.title: She thinks she is allowed, like the ox at the threshing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the wife does not see her taking as stealing. So nothing can be learned from her about swapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: There too, she rules for herself and says: 'The ox eats from its threshing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes away the proof from step 1. He shows that her taking is not real, knowing theft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She thinks that a person who works with food may eat from it, just like an ox that is allowed to eat while threshing. Her taking comes from a mistaken היתר, not from being a thief. So there is no basis to say every עם הארץ would knowingly swap food.

keyTerms.meaning: she rules for herself (decides it is allowed)
the ox eats from its threshing

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
There too, she rules for herself and says:
The ox eats from its threshing.
phrases.notes: This is based on the פסוק about not muzzling an ox while it threshes: דברים 25:4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יוסף התם נמי מוריא ואמרה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that every עם הארץ is suspected of swapping food
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Her taking is not knowing theft. She believes she is allowed to take, so her case teaches nothing about swapping.
steps.whatToRemember: The wife's taking does not prove that every עם הארץ swaps food. She takes only because she thinks she is allowed, like an ox eating while it threshes.

steps.title: Preparing the עם הארץ's dough and its חלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a חבר may not prepare an עם הארץ's חלה in purity. He may prepare the plain dough in purity, set aside the amount of חלה, and let the עם הארץ take both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן המשולם testified in the name of his brother רבי יוחנן, who said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן חסמא: One may not prepare the חלה of an עם הארץ in purity. But one may prepare his plain dough in purity, take from it the amount of חלה, and put it in a basket or container. When the עם הארץ comes to take, he takes both, and the preparer need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It teaches how a חבר may knead dough for an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Preparing the חלה itself in purity for the עם הארץ is not allowed. There is a permitted way around this: knead the whole plain dough in purity, then separate the חלה amount and set it aside in a container. After that, the עם הארץ may take both pieces, and the חבר does not need to worry about what happens to them.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of dough given to a כֹּהֵן
an ordinary person not careful about purity and tithes
in a state of ritual purity

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam testified
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, his brother,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַסָּמָא:
phrases.english: who said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Chasma:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין חַלַּת עַם הָאָרֶץ בְּטׇהֳרָה,
phrases.english: One may not prepare the challa of an am ha'aretz in purity,
but one may prepare his ordinary dough in purity;
and he takes from it the amount of challa,
and places it in a basket or a container;
phrases.notes: These are kinds of containers that don't pick up טומאה, so the חלה stays pure in them.

phrases.english: and when the am ha'aretz comes to take,
he takes both of them, and he need not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: העיד רבי יוסי בן המשולם משום רבי יוחנן אחיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: helping an עם הארץ with his holy portions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חבר may not prepare an עם הארץ's חלה in purity. He may prepare the plain dough in purity and set aside the חלה, and then the עם הארץ may take both.

steps.title: The same rule for olives and תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats the same pattern for olive oil. A חבר may not prepare an עם הארץ's תרומה in purity, but may press the plain olives in purity, set aside תרומה in his own vessel, and let the עם הארץ take both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not prepare the תרומה of his olives in purity. But one may prepare his ordinary olives in purity, take from them the amount of תרומה, and put it in the חבר's vessel. When the עם הארץ comes to take, he takes both, and the preparer need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, matching case. This time it is about olives and תרומה instead of dough and חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule works exactly like the dough case. The only change is the container: the תרומה goes into the חבר's own vessel. The ending is the same, too: the עם הארץ takes both, and the חבר need not worry.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן
the vessel belonging to the חבר
a person careful about purity and tithes

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases the חבר may not prepare the holy portion itself in purity for the עם הארץ. He may prepare the plain food in purity, set the holy portion aside in a container, and let the עם הארץ take both without worry.

phrases.english: And one may not prepare the teruma of his olives in purity,
but one may prepare his ordinary olives in purity;
and he takes from it the amount of teruma,
and places it in the vessel of the chaver;
and when the am ha'aretz comes to take,
he takes both of them, and he need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel second case within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חבר may not prepare an עם הארץ's תרומה in purity. He may press the plain olives in purity and set aside תרומה in his own vessel, and then the עם הארץ may take both.

steps.title: Why was this allowed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's permission for a חבר to work on an עם הארץ's dough and olives.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why חכמים allowed a חבר to prepare the עם הארץ's dough and olives in purity. This question sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא let the חבר do part of the work even though he may not prepare the חלה or תרומה itself. The גמרא wants to know what reason justifies this permission.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא quoted in steps 3 and 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason חכמים allowed a חבר to prepare an עם הארץ's dough and olives in purity

steps.title: To protect the workers' livelihood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the permission was given so the kneader and the olive presser can earn a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because of the kneader's livelihood, and because of the olive presser's livelihood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question: חכמים were lenient so that a חבר who kneads dough or presses olives for a living does not lose his income.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חבר could never work for an עם הארץ, he would lose many customers. So חכמים allowed him to do the plain work in purity, as long as he does not prepare the holy portion itself.

keyTerms.meaning: His livelihood, what he needs to live

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Because of the livelihood of the kneader,
and because of the livelihood of the olive presser.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The permission exists to protect the livelihood of kneaders and olive pressers

steps.title: Why both the kneader and the presser had to be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we could not learn the kneader from the presser or the presser from the kneader, so both cases were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If we were taught only the kneader, we might say the leniency is because he earns little, but the olive presser, who earns a lot, would not get it. If we were taught only the olive presser, we might say the leniency is because his work is not common, but the kneader, whose work is common, would not get it. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא had to give both cases, dough and olives, instead of just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each worker has a special reason to need help. The kneader earns little, and the olive presser only has work in olive season. Since each reason applies to only one of them, we could not learn one case from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary to state both cases
I might say no, it does not apply

steps.confusionAlert: Each reason makes the OTHER worker look like he doesn't need the leniency. The kneader earns little, so the presser who earns more might seem not to need it. The presser's work is rare, so the kneader whose work is steady might seem not to need it.

phrases.english: And it is necessary;
for if it had taught us only the kneader,
that is because his pay is not large,
but an olive presser, whose pay is large,
I would say no.
And if it had taught us only the olive presser,
that is because his work is not common,
phrases.notes: Olive pressing only happens in olive season, so he has fewer chances to earn.

phrases.english: but a kneader, whose work is common,
I would say no; so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's reason to show why the ברייתא needed both cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both cases are needed because each worker has his own reason for needing the leniency, and neither reason covers the other

steps.title: The ברייתא again: the עם הארץ takes both dough and חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the line of the ברייתא saying the עם הארץ may carry away both the dough and the separated חלה. It does this so it can examine that line in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He takes the amount of חלה from it and puts it in a basket or a vessel; and when the עם הארץ comes to take it, he takes both, and the חבר does not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote one line of the ברייתא. This sets up a question about that line in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חבר sets aside the חלה in a container that does not become impure, and then lets the עם הארץ carry everything home. The detail the גמרא will examine is the phrase 'he does not worry.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; used to quote again a source already brought
He does not need to worry

phrases.english: The Master said:
He takes from it the amount of חלה,
and places it in a basket or a vessel;
and when the עם הארץ comes to take it,
he takes both of them, and he does not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: נוֹטֵל הֵימֶנָּה כְּדֵי חַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 3 to examine one detail
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עם הארץ may take both the dough and the separated חלה, and the חבר need not worry

steps.title: Maybe the עם הארץ will touch the חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: we should worry that the עם הארץ will touch the חלה and make it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe he will touch it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the words 'he does not worry.' An עם הארץ is treated as impure, so if he touches the חלה it will become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point was to keep the חלה pure. Handing it to the עם הארץ seems to put it right back in danger.

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he will touch it!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the חלה. If the עם הארץ touches it, it becomes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling quoted in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the חבר need not worry when the עם הארץ takes the חלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עם הארץ might touch the חלה and make it impure, which defeats the purpose of preparing it in purity

steps.title: We warn him not to touch it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we warn the עם הארץ that if he touches the חלה, his dough goes back to being טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we say to him: Look, if you touch it, it goes back to being טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we give the עם הארץ a warning that keeps him from touching the חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning makes it his own problem. If he touches the חלה, his dough is treated as untithed again and he cannot eat it, so he will be careful.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes back to being טבל, untithed food that may not be eaten

phrases.english: Because we say to him:
Look, if you touch it,
it goes back to being טבל.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ: חֲזִי, אִי נָגְעַתְּ בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical safeguard: a warning that keeps the danger from happening
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Handing the חלה to an עם הארץ puts it at risk of becoming impure
steps.terutzMaskana: The warning that the dough becomes טבל again keeps him from touching it

steps.title: Maybe he doesn't care
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: maybe the עם הארץ does not care whether his dough becomes טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe he does not care!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. A warning only works if the person cares about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is not careful about these laws. So he might ignore the warning and touch the חלה anyway.

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he does not care!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the warning will stop the עם הארץ from touching the חלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A warning is useless if the עם הארץ does not care whether his dough is טבל

steps.title: He clearly wants to do it right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this עם הארץ obviously cares, because he went out of his way to have his dough prepared properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, he is trying to prepare it properly. Would he not care?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this particular עם הארץ shows he cares, since he hired a חבר to prepare his food in purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His actions prove what he wants. Someone who went to the trouble of hiring a pure worker will not throw it all away by touching the חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Now; used to argue 'since this is so, how could that be?'

steps.whatToRemember: A חבר may do the plain work for an עם הארץ to protect his livelihood, and the עם הארץ may carry home the pure חלה. We trust him because we warn him, and because hiring a pure worker shows he cares.

phrases.english: Now, he is trying to prepare it properly;
would he really not care?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 and closes the discussion
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from behavior: his actions show he cares
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An עם הארץ might ignore the warning because he does not care
steps.terutzMaskana: This עם הארץ hired a pure worker, which proves he cares and will listen to the warning

steps.title: The oil case: the עם הארץ takes both the oil and the תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. The olive presser sets aside the תרומה oil in a חבר's vessel, and the עם הארץ may take both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He takes the amount needed for תרומה from the oil and puts it in a vessel belonging to a חבר. When the עם הארץ comes to collect, he takes both, and the presser does not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the oil case from the same ברייתא. This sets up a question just like the one it asked about the חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in the dough case, the ברייתא let the עם הארץ carry both the dough and the חלה. Here it gives the same ruling for oil: the תרומה is separated into a pure vessel, and the עם הארץ may take everything home.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', a formula that quotes an earlier source again in order to discuss it
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be kept pure
Someone careful about the laws of purity

phrases.english: The Master said:
He takes from it the amount for teruma,
phrases.notes: 'It' here is the oil at the olive press, the next case in the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: and places it in the vessel of a ḥaver;
and when the am ha'aretz comes to take,
he takes both of them, and he is not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: נוֹטֵל הֵימֶנָּה כְּדֵי תְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dough case to the parallel oil case in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The presser puts the תרומה oil in a חבר's vessel, and the עם הארץ may take both the oil and the תרומה.

steps.title: How will the עם הארץ know not to touch the oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא worries the עם הארץ will touch the תרומה oil. With the חלה there was a clear sign, but here there seems to be none.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that he will touch it! Granted, in the חלה case there is a clear sign. Here, what sign is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the oil ruling. Unlike the חלה, there seems to be nothing that shows the עם הארץ which part is תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the חלה, a special container marked it out, so the warning made sense. With oil, everything looks the same, so the עם הארץ might touch the תרומה without realizing it and make it impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; it makes sense in one case, but not the other

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he will touch it!
Granted there, he has a marker;
phrases.notes: 'There' is the חלה case from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: here, what marker does he have?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the oil ruling from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the עם הארץ may take both the oil and the תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a visible marker, the עם הארץ may touch the תרומה oil and make it impure.

steps.title: The oil is put in vessels that cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: The תרומה oil is placed in vessels made of dung, stone, or earth, which cannot become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He puts it in dung vessels, stone vessels, or earth vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the presser uses special vessels for the תרומה oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These kinds of vessels cannot become impure, so the oil inside stays protected. They are also unusual for oil, so they serve as the marker that tells the עם הארץ which part is תרומה.

phrases.english: He places it in dung vessels,
in stone vessels, in earth vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oil sits in an ordinary vessel with no marker, so it is at risk.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oil is in special vessels that cannot become impure, which keeps it safe and also marks it.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא mention a חבר's vessel?
steps.stepSummary: If the protection comes from the type of vessel, it should not matter whether the vessel belongs to a חבר or to an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why specifically a חבר's vessel? Even one belonging to an עם הארץ would work too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא based on the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stone, dung, and earth vessels never become impure, no matter who owns them. So the words 'of a חבר' in the ברייתא seem unnecessary.

phrases.english: If so, why specifically those of a ḥaver?
Even those of an am ha'aretz too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 15 to question the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'בְּכִלְיוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If what protects the oil is the material of the vessel, the owner should make no difference.

steps.title: It means the עם הארץ's vessels that a חבר could use
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means vessels of the עם הארץ that are fit for a חבר, because they cannot become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what it means: vessels of the עם הארץ that a חבר could use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the challenge and explains how to read the ברייתא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A חבר's vessel' does not mean a vessel he owns. It means a type of vessel a חבר would be willing to use, and that includes the עם הארץ's own stone, dung, or earth vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed what it is saying

phrases.english: This is also what he is saying:
in vessels of the am ha'aretz,
that are fit for a ḥaver to use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by explaining the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A חבר's vessel' means a vessel the חבר owns.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means any vessel fit for a חבר, even one owned by the עם הארץ.
steps.whatToRemember: The תרומה oil is safe because of the type of vessel, not because of who owns it.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: encouraging גוים during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one may 'strengthen the hands' of גוים during שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may strengthen the hands of גוים during שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי working the land during שביעית is not bound by its rules. The משנה says a Jew may 'strengthen his hands', but it does not explain what that means. The next step will challenge it.

keyTerms.meaning: Strengthen the hands of; support or encourage
The seventh year, when working the land is forbidden

phrases.english: One may strengthen the hands of gentiles in the Seventh Year:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may strengthen the hands of גוים working the land during שביעית.

steps.title: But רב said not to hoe with a גוי during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב taught that one may not hoe with a גוי during שביעית, and may not say 'שלום' to a גוי twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: May one really help them? But רב דימי בר שישנא said in the name of רב: one may not hoe with a גוי during שביעית, and one may not double 'שלום' to a גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a statement of רב that seems to forbid helping a גוי during שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'strengthening' means actually helping with the work, it contradicts רב's ban on hoeing together with a גוי. The second half of רב's statement, about doubling 'שלום', will come up again in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? Introduces a contradicting source

phrases.english: May one strengthen?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר שִׁישְׁנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Dimi bar Shishna say in the name of Rav:
One may not hoe with the gentile in the Seventh Year,
and one may not double "shalom" to a gentile!
phrases.notes: He means saying "shalom, shalom" to a גוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְזִיקִין?! וְהָאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר שִׁישְׁנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to strengthen the hands of גוים during שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids hoeing with a גוי during שביעית, so how can the משנה allow helping him?

steps.title: The משנה only allows words of encouragement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means only saying 'Be strong' to them, as רב יהודה and רב ששת did.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is needed to teach that one may just say 'Be strong' to them. That is like רב יהודה, who said to them 'Be strong', and רב ששת, who said to them 'Well done'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'strengthening' means encouraging words, not actual help with the work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hoeing together with a גוי is real help and stays forbidden. A friendly word of encouragement is allowed. The גמרא backs this up with what two אמוראים actually said.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed only for this case

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
to merely say to them "Be strong" —

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אֲמַר לְהוּ ״אַחְזוּקוּ״;
phrases.english: like that of Rav Yehuda, who said to them "Be strong";
Rav Sheshet said to them "Well done."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Strengthening' means actually helping with the work.
steps.whatToRemember: During שביעית, you may not work alongside a גוי, but you may wish him well.

steps.title: How רב חסדא and רב כהנא avoided saying 'שלום' twice
steps.stepSummary: Going back to רב's rule about not doubling 'שלום', the גמרא shows how two אמוראים handled it: רב חסדא greeted first, and רב כהנא answered 'שלמא למר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'one may not double שלום to a גוי': רב חסדא would greet them first. רב כהנא would say to them 'Peace to the master.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of רב's statement and shows how two אמוראים put it into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who is greeted answers with a stronger greeting. רב חסדא greeted first, so he never had to answer with a doubled 'שלום'. רב כהנא answered with 'peace to the master' instead of repeating 'שלום'.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes first; greets before the other person

phrases.english: And one may not double "shalom" to a gentile:

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא מַקְדֵּים וְיָהֵיב לְהוּ שְׁלָמָא.
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda would go first and give them a greeting.
Rav Kahana would say to them "Peace to the master."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the second half of רב's statement from step 19 and shows how it was practiced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two ways to avoid doubling 'שלום' to a גוי: greet him first, or answer 'שלמא למר'.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule against doubling 'שלום' was kept by greeting first (רב חסדא) or by answering 'שלמא למר' (רב כהנא).

steps.title: The משנה allows greeting גוים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: one may ask after the welfare of גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and we may greet them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, that we may greet גוים for the sake of peace. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא discussed 'strengthening the hands' of גוים. Now it quotes the next part of the same משנה so it can examine it.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask after their welfare, meaning we greet them

phrases.english: And we may greet them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same משנה quoted in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may greet גוים for the sake of peace.

steps.title: Why say greeting is allowed if helping is already allowed?
steps.stepSummary: If we may already 'strengthen' גוים, it seems obvious that we may greet them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that we already strengthen them, do we really need to be told that we may greet them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers to say we may greet גוים. It already said we may strengthen their hands, which seems like a bigger thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'why say the obvious?' challenge. If the bigger allowance (encouraging them) is permitted, the smaller one (a greeting) should go without saying. So this extra line in the משנה looks unnecessary.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Strengthening' here goes back to Steps 18 and 20, where it was limited to saying 'Be strong' to them. It is not a new idea.

phrases.english: Now that we already strengthen them,
is it necessary to say that we may greet them?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא אַחְזוֹקֵי מַחְזְקִינַן, שׁוֹאֲלִין בִּשְׁלוֹמָן מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the clause just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the bigger allowance of strengthening them is already given, the smaller allowance of greeting them looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The rule is needed for their holiday
steps.stepSummary: רב ייבא says the clause teaches about greeting on the גוי's holiday, which needs special care.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ייבא said: it is needed only for their holiday. A ברייתא teaches that a person should not go into a גוי's house on his holiday and greet him. If he meets him in the market, he greets him quietly and seriously.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ייבא answers that the משנה's rule is about greeting a גוי on his holiday. He supports this with a ברייתא that explains how such a greeting must be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On their holiday, a greeting could look like you are joining their celebration. So you may not go to his house to greet him, but if you meet him by chance in the market you may greet him in a low voice and a serious tone. The משנה's 'we may greet them' is teaching that even on that day a greeting is allowed in this limited way.
steps.whatToRemember: Greeting a גוי is allowed for peace. On his holiday, though, do not visit his home to greet him. If you meet him in the market, greet him quietly and seriously.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even an allowed act of friendliness has limits when it could look like honoring a foreign holiday.

phrases.english: Rav Yeiva said:
It was needed only for their holiday –
as it was taught: A person may not enter the house
of a גוי on his holiday,
and greet him with 'שלום'.
If he met him in the market –
he greets him in a quiet voice
and in a serious manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יֵיבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְיוֹם אֵידָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case the משנה is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (the clause teaches about a special day)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought that greeting on their holiday is completely forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even on their holiday a greeting is allowed, but only quietly, seriously, and not by going to his house.

steps.title: Should we stand up for גניבא?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא see the scholar גניבא pass by and argue over whether to stand for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא were sitting. גניבא was passing by. One said to the other: Let us stand before him, for he is a Torah scholar. The other said: Should we stand before a quarrelsome person?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the topic of doubling 'שלום.' Two אמוראים argue about whether to honor גניבא by standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says his Torah learning earns him respect. The other side says his habit of fighting takes that respect away. This sets the scene for גניבא's greeting in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A scholar of that time, known for being involved in disputes
A son of Torah, a Torah scholar

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי.
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda were sitting.
Geneiva was passing by,
one said to his friend:
Let us stand before him, for he is a Torah scholar.
He said to him: And should we stand before a quarrelsome person?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story connected to the earlier theme of doubling 'שלום' (Steps 19 and 21).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: a disagreement about whether to honor a scholar who is quarrelsome.

steps.title: גניבא greets them twice as 'kings'
steps.stepSummary: גניבא comes over and says 'Peace upon you, kings' two times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, he came over to them and said: Peace upon you, kings! Peace upon you, kings!
steps.whatsHappening: גניבא arrives and greets the two rabbis with a doubled 'שלום,' calling them kings. This greeting sets up their two questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two unusual things in his greeting: he calls rabbis 'kings,' and he says 'שלום' twice. Each of these will be questioned and given a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of this

phrases.english: Meanwhile, he came over to them,
he said to them: Peace upon you, kings,
peace upon you, kings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story; גניבא reaches them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גניבא greets the rabbis with a doubled 'שלום' and calls them kings.

steps.title: Why call rabbis 'kings'?
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis ask גניבא for his source that Torah scholars are called kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: From where do you know that rabbis are called kings?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא and רב חסדא ask גניבא to explain the first part of his greeting: calling them kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real request for a source, not an attack. They want to know what gives Torah scholars the title of 'kings.'

phrases.english: They said to him: From where do you know
that rabbis are called kings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מְנָא לָךְ דְּרַבָּנַן אִיקְּרוּ מְלָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first part of גניבא's greeting.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that Torah scholars are called kings.

steps.title: 'Through me kings rule'
steps.stepSummary: גניבא brings the פסוק in משלי where the Torah says 'through me kings rule.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: As it is written: 'Through me kings rule...'
steps.whatsHappening: גניבא answers with a פסוק in which the Torah speaks and says that kings rule through it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק the speaker is the Torah, so the people who rule 'through' the Torah are its scholars. That is why rabbis can be called kings.

phrases.english: He said to them: As it is written:
'Through me kings rule, etc.'
phrases.notes: משלי 8:15. 'Me' here is the Torah speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דִּכְתִיב: בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלוֹכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about calling rabbis kings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'בי מלכים ימלוכו' shows that those who rule through Torah are called kings.

steps.title: Why double 'שלום' for kings?
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis ask for a source for saying 'שלום' twice to a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: And from where do you know that we say 'שלום' twice to kings?
steps.whatsHappening: Now they ask about the second part of his greeting: saying 'שלום' twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב said not to double 'שלום' to a גוי (Step 19). So a doubled 'שלום' is a special greeting, and they want to know who deserves it.

phrases.english: They said to him: And from where do you know
that we double 'שלום' to kings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וּמְנָא לָךְ דְּכָפְלִינַן שְׁלָמָא לְמַלְכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second part of גניבא's greeting.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for greeting a king with a doubled 'שלום'.

steps.title: עמשי's doubled greeting to דוד
steps.stepSummary: גניבא quotes רב יהודה in the name of רב, who learns the doubled greeting from עמשי's words to דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: From where do we know that we double 'שלום' to a king? As it says: 'And a spirit clothed עמשי, the chief of the captains...'
steps.whatsHappening: גניבא answers with a teaching of רב: the doubled 'שלום' for a king comes from the פסוק where עמשי greets דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of that פסוק, hinted at by 'etc.,' says 'שלום שלום לך' to דוד, the king. So a king is greeted with a double 'שלום,' and rabbis, who are called kings, get the same greeting.

keyTerms.meaning: עמשי, a leader who joined דוד

steps.whatToRemember: Rabbis are called kings, based on 'בי מלכים ימלוכו.' Kings get a doubled 'שלום,' based on עמשי's greeting to דוד.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: He said to them: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that we double 'שלום' to a king?
As it says: 'And a spirit clothed Amasai,
the chief of the captains, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 12:19. The 'etc.' points to the end of the פסוק: 'שלום שלום לך,' said to דוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about doubling 'שלום'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב learns from עמשי's 'שלום שלום' to דוד that a king is greeted with a doubled 'שלום'.

steps.title: They invite גניבא to eat
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis offer גניבא something to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Would the master like to taste something?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the rabbis politely invite גניבא to eat. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a friendly offer, not a challenge. It gives גניבא a chance to share another teaching of רב.

phrases.english: They said to him: Let the master taste something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the greeting discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: an invitation to eat.

steps.title: Feed your animal before you eat
steps.stepSummary: גניבא declines, quoting רב: one may not eat before feeding his animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: So said רב יהודה in the name of רב: A person may not taste anything until he gives food to his animal. As it says: 'And I will give grass in your field for your animal,' and only afterward: 'and you will eat and be satisfied.'
steps.whatsHappening: גניבא turns down the food, explaining that he has not yet fed his animal. He quotes רב's rule that the animal must be fed first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule comes from the order of the פסוק: first the animal's grass is mentioned, then 'you will eat.' Since גניבא's animal had not eaten yet, he could not eat either.

keyTerms.meaning: And you will eat and be satisfied

steps.whatToRemember: A person may not eat until he has fed his animals. This is learned from the order of the פסוק in דברים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה about caring for animals that people still follow today.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: He said to them: So said Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav:
It is forbidden for a person to taste anything
until he gives food to his animal,
as it says: 'And I will give grass in your field for your animal,'
and afterward: 'and you will eat and be satisfied.'
phrases.notes: The animal is mentioned first, so it eats first. גניבא hadn't fed his yet, so he couldn't eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָסוּר לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁיִּטְעוֹם כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the invitation by turning it down with a halachic reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He cannot eat yet, because רב rules that a person must feed his animal before eating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may not taste anything until he has fed his animal, learned from the order of the פסוק: 'ונתתי עשב בשדך לבהמתך' and then 'ואכלת ושבעת'.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הניזקין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes פרק הניזקין with the traditional הדרן line, promising to return to this chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הניזקין.
steps.whatsHappening: There is no new discussion here. The chapter is over, and this is the traditional closing line said when finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הדרן עלך mean 'we will return to you.' They show love for the learning and a promise to review it, so the chapter is never really left behind. The chapter is named הניזקין after the opening word of its first משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing line said at the end of every chapter.
Damaged parties. This is the first word of the chapter's opening משנה, so it is the chapter's name.
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא.

steps.whatToRemember: פרק הניזקין is now finished. The הדרן line is a promise to come back and review it, and it is not part of the legal discussion.
steps.confusionAlert: This line does not teach a new הלכה. It just marks the end of the chapter, so do not try to connect it to גניבא's last statement.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter HaNizakin

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the story of גניבא (steps 25-32) ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק הניזקין is complete, and we commit to returning to review it.
